title: Κεφάλαιον Βʹ — Ὁ Κῆπος καὶ Τὰ Ζῷα
titleTranslation: Chapter 2 — The Garden and the Animals

paragraphs.label: Μέρος Αʹ — Ὁ Κῆπος (Part A — The Garden)
paragraphs.translation: There is a garden. The garden is beautiful. The farmer has the garden. The garden is small, but beautiful. The garden is near the house.
There is a vegetable in the garden. The farmer plants the vegetable in the garden and takes the vegetable and eats in the house.

There is a tree in the field. The tree is large. Fruits are on the tree; the fruits of the tree are beautiful. And branches are on the tree. The tree has the branches and the branches bear the fruits.
There is a sickle. The farmer has a sickle. So he takes the sickle and harvests the fruits from the tree and carries them toward the house.
There is a donkey in the farmer's field. The donkey carries the stones out of the field. The donkey is good. There is also an ox in the field. The ox is great and strong.
There is a sheep. The sheep is an animal. And the animals are in the field. The sheep stays in the field and eats the grass of the field and drinks from the river.
The sheep has a lamb. The lamb is the offspring of the sheep and is small. And the lamb runs quickly in the field. The farmer sees the lamb and the sheep in the field and rejoices.
The river flows near the field. And across the river there is a wild beast. The wolf is a wild beast. The wolf is large. The farmer sees the wolf across the river. He does not rejoice.
For the wolf sees the lamb and the sheep in the field. The ox is great and strong, but the lamb is small. The wolf does not look at the ox, but the lamb.

paragraphs.label: Ὁ Γεωργὸς Λέγει — The Farmer Speaks
paragraphs.translation: The farmer says: 'I have a beautiful garden near the house. There is a vegetable in the garden. I also have the great tree in the field. On the tree there are fruits and branches. I take the sickle and harvest the fruits from the tree. The donkey carries the fruits toward the house. The donkey is good. I also have a strong ox in the field. I have a sheep and a lamb. But now I see the wolf across the river. The wolf does not see the great ox; he sees the small lamb. God is good and guards the lamb. I give thanks to God.'

paragraphs.label: Μέρος Βʹ — Ὁ Λύκος (Part B — The Wolf)
paragraphs.translation: The day is beautiful. The sun shines in the sky. The river flows beautifully.
The sheep eats the grass of the field. The lamb runs on the grass and rejoices. The ox stays in the field. The farmer sits outside the house and rests.
The wolf stays across the river and sees the sheep and the lamb. For the wolf wants to seize the lamb and eat it. The wolf is evil.
The sheep and the lamb do not see the wolf. For the sheep eats the grass and the lamb runs on the grass.
The farmer sees the wolf across the river and does not rejoice. For the farmer loves the sheep and the lamb. He is therefore about to save the sheep and the lamb from the wolf.
For the good farmer does not abandon his animals and flee from the wild beast. But he stays and guards his animals.
And look! The wolf runs into the river and comes out of the river into the field. Now he is near the lamb. For he wants and is about to seize it.

The lamb does not see the wolf. But the donkey hears the wolf and cries out. Immediately the farmer takes his rod. He also takes stones from the field. He runs into the field and cries out with a great voice. He throws the stones at the wolf.

He cries out again and says: 'Go away from the field!' The wolf hears the farmer's voice and sees the stones and the rod. He is no longer about to seize the lamb. He does not want to stay in the field. So he flees from the lamb toward the river.
The farmer pursues the wolf and cries out again and throws stones again. Finally the wolf flees across the river.
The farmer stays in the field and sees his animals. The sheep eats the grass. The lamb runs on the grass. The ox stays in the field. The donkey rests. Therefore the farmer rejoices.

paragraphs.label: Ὁ Γεωργὸς Εὐχαριστεῖ — The Farmer Gives Thanks
paragraphs.translation: So the farmer sits on the stone under the tree and gives thanks to God. He says: 'O Lord my God. I give thanks to you. You are righteous and faithful. You love me and my animals. Today you guard me and my animals. The wolf wants to seize the lamb, but you save it from the wolf. You are great and good.'
Then the farmer calls the sheep and the lamb. The sheep knows the farmer's voice. The lamb also knows his voice. For they hear his voice every day.
So the farmer lifts the lamb and carries it. The sheep follows. The donkey carries the fruits of the tree. They go out of the field. The farmer leads his animals toward the house.

titleTranslations.es: Capítulo 2 — El Jardín y los Animales
